title: Differential compatibility tier against a real Jellyfin 12.4
description: Run jellyfin/jellyfin:12.4 and jellyscale side by side over the same fixtures, replay the same requests to both, and diff normalized responses (JSON with ids, timestamps and ordering normalized; headers; HLS playlists). Intentional improvements on Jellyfin go in an allowlist with a reason each. This is the project plan's jfdiff, never built.
acceptanceCriteria: A test tier starts a disposable Jellyfin 12.4 on a Docker-assigned port over the e2e fixtures and diffs every route the tier knows
Normalization of ids, tokens, timestamps and ordering is explicit and tested
An allowlist file lists each intentional deviation with its reason; an unlisted difference fails
Shows the Continue Reading bug of PR #32 as a diff when the fix is reverted
Runs in CI (sharded if needed) and locally; docs/testing.md explains adding a route
Later compatibility tasks can state acceptance as 'route X matches, apart from the allowlist'
notes: Evidence: agents converge when they can loop against a known-good reference (Anthropic's C compiler diffed against GCC; Ladybird's LibJS port held byte-identical output and passed 52,898 test262 tests; Airbnb and Google migrations verified every step). Compatibility with unmodified clients is jellyscale's top risk, and today it is checked only by hand-made captures and jellyfin-web in Playwright.
